claims.text: Increasing laser scanning speed during LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi increases the effective cooling rate and promotes rapid solidification.
Rapid solidification and high cooling rates inhibit grain growth and refine the microstructure.
Rapid solidification reduces elemental segregation by limiting the time available for redistribution.
Increasing laser scanning speed reduces the development of thermal gradients.
High-speed LPBF produces finer grains and fewer segregated grain-boundary regions in AlCrFeNiSi than slower-speed LPBF or bulk fabrication.
Increasing laser scanning speed lowers residual stress in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
Increasing laser scanning speed reduces processing-induced defect density in LPBF AlCrFeNiSi.
A refined, less segregated microstructure with lower residual stress and fewer defects improves mechanical performance.
Higher-speed LPBF increases the yield strength of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional processing.
Higher-speed LPBF increases the ductility of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional processing.
Conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi has a coarser microstructure than LPBF material.
Conventionally bulk-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi exhibits appreciable elemental segregation.
Slower-speed LPBF or bulk fabrication of AlCrFeNiSi produces greater residual stress than higher-speed LPBF.
Laser power and powder thermal properties can alter the outcome of the scanning-speed intervention.

contradictions.description: The conditions and experiment require scanning speed to be the only changed variable, but the baseline also permits comparison with bulk-fabricated material. A bulk-versus-LPBF comparison necessarily changes the fabrication route and many parameters in addition to scanning speed.
